readme: recipe-floor-id -> board-commodity-id mappings for derive-recipe-floors.ps1. EVERY entry is a ONE-TIME HUMAN VERIFICATION that the two ids are the SAME commodity in the SAME form (fresh vs frozen, block vs shredded, plain vs seasoned all count as DIFFERENT). A verified entry automates that row's monthly floor refresh forever; a wrong one silently prices the floor off a different product (the board-collision class). Add entries as the monthly agent hand-checks the no-board-match list; include reviewed dates.
review_log: 2026-07-23: 16 mappings accepted from propose-floor-id-map.ps1 evidence gate (full label-token match + unit reconciliation + multi-store price agreement <=25%) with human review of each; REJECTED olives->olive-oil (single-token false positive, different product) - see out/floor-id-map-proposals.json for the evidence rows. pepperoncini->banana-peppers verified intentional: the board commodity label is literally Banana Peppers / Pepperoncini. ROUND 2 (2026-07-23): 17 more accepted via curated price-test (>=2-store everyday agreement + form review). REJECTED with evidence: boneless-skinless-chicken-thigh->chicken-thighs (board=bone-in drumstick pricing, 1/6), jasmine-rice->rice (0/6, jasmine pricier), salsa-verde->salsa (1/5), seasoned-black-beans->canned-black-beans (1/4), 93-7-ground-turkey->ground-turkey (3 stores cheapest = fattier grind, would understate), red-bell-pepper->bell-peppers (board cheapest = green), zero-sugar-soda-2l->soda (2L vs 12-pack economics), frozen-broccoli-florets->frozen-broccoli (cuts-vs-florets understating risk). apple->apples accepted on identity; its each-vs-lb unit mismatch is the deriver's refusal flow, safe.
